sections.heading: RB-3 Roll-forward and rate base at 31 December
sections.body:
3. The rate base is $1,072.6M at 31 December 2026, $295.7M (38.1%) above the $776.9M allowed in 2025.
Net plant of $1,075.2M at 30 September, plus $173.3M of fourth-quarter additions and $6.8M of completed construction, less $9.3M of fourth-quarter depreciation, gives $1,246.0M. Less contributions, deferred taxes and advances ($192.9M), plus cash working capital and materials ($19.5M). At the allowed return that is about $31.3M a year of revenue requirement. The 2026 depreciation study would lower the rate base by $2.4M, but it is not filed and the schedules use the approved rates.

sections.heading: What is taken out or held, and why
sections.body:
Present $1,072.6M: the 31 on-track additions in, the seven dated 2027 out and listed for the next case (preferred)
Schedules RB-1 to RB-5 at 31 December 2026 at the approved depreciation rates, with the nine completed projects counted as completed construction and the two prudence gaps closed before the 4 November session. The seven go on a separate list for the next case, each with the date it could come back in.
Rate base: $1,072.6M · Since 2025: +$295.7M · 38.1% · Held for next case: $41.3M · 7 projects · Prudence gaps: 2 · $34.1M
Trade-off: About $4.4M a year of revenue waits for the next case, but nothing in the filing rests on a date the project managers have not confirmed.

Present all 38 as filed, $1,113.9M, and update when the project managers confirm
Keep the seven in the schedules until the 6 November confirmations, then take out any still dated 2027 in the 13 November update.
Rate base: $1,113.9M · Rests on: 6 unconfirmed dates · Revision after filing: likely · Revenue at stake: $4.4M a year
Trade-off: Keeps the revenue in the filing for now, but staff see a figure the order says will come down, and one project manager has already confirmed the slip.

Hold the schedules until the 6 November close and the confirmations
Wait for Plant Accounting to move the nine and for the project managers to answer, then file schedules where every figure is booked and confirmed.
Every figure: booked and confirmed · Schedules ready: ~9 Nov · Marc’s date: 30 Oct missed · Review before 13 Nov: 4 days
Trade-off: The cleanest record, but Marc goes into the 4 November session without schedules, and the update gets four days of review.

session.title: Off-framework order note: the 20 October load
session.audience: Tolu Adeyemi, Head of Capital Procurement, and the nine project managers
session.purpose: Re-place the nine unconfirmed lines on the frameworks before the suppliers confirm them

fromGoal.title: Procurement spend 2.5% lower: check every new order against the frameworks

sections.heading: What we ask, and by when
sections.body:
Re-place the nine unconfirmed lines on the frameworks before the suppliers confirm them.

Goal: Take 2.5% off capital procurement spend across all projects. Check every new order line against the framework agreements and the category benchmarks; when lines go off-framework or above benchmark, size the premium, find out why, and come back with what can still be done before the orders ship, or say plainly that nothing can.
Decision asked: Re-place the off-framework lines on the frameworks, and fix what sent them there
Deadline: Before the suppliers confirm the nine open lines, usually within two working days

sections.heading: The lines and their premium
sections.body:
1. 14 of the 31 lines in the 20 October load are off-framework: $3.86M ordered, $0.55M (16.8%) above framework prices.

sections.heading: Why it happened
sections.body:
1. 14 of the 31 lines in the 20 October load are off-framework: $3.86M ordered, $0.55M (16.8%) above framework prices.
All 14 are ductile iron pipe, fittings, gate valves and hydrants on nine network blanket projects in Lakeshore and Eastmoor, ordered from two spot suppliers, Northgate Supply Co. and Ridgeline Waterworks Supply. Every item is on FA-2025-PIPE-01 or FA-2025-VLV-02. Nine lines ($2.04M ordered, $0.30M of the premium) are not yet confirmed by the supplier.

2. It started in April, when Harbor Pipe’s lead time reached 11 weeks, and it did not stop when the lead time came back.
Since April $11.4M of orders went off-framework or above benchmark, $1.37M over the framework and benchmark prices and most of it pipe and valves: a run rate of about $2.6M a year. Harbor Pipe has been back to 4 weeks since 29 September, but the ordering catalogue still defaults to the spot suppliers, so new orders land there unless someone changes the supplier by hand.

3. Line by line the premium is 15% to 18% on every item, and none of the 14 orders carries the exception the policy requires.
Gate valves 12 in at $3,820.72 against $3,260.00 (17.2%); ductile iron 12 in at $70.87 and $71.48 per foot against $61.20; hydrants at $4,664.95 against $3,950.00 (18.1%). Every line is above $25k, so the policy puts it on the framework unless Procurement records an exception. None is recorded.

4. Nine lines can still be re-placed at no cost; the five confirmed lines would carry up to 5% restocking.
The policy lets an unconfirmed line be cancelled at no cost. Re-placing the nine on the frameworks keeps $0.30M and brings the program to $9.0M of $24.2M (37.2%). The five confirmed lines ($1.82M ordered, $0.26M of premium) could come back only with the suppliers’ agreement, at up to $0.09M of restocking.

visual.title: Premium paid off-framework, by category, April to September
visual.note: Pipe and valves carry most of it: the two categories where the catalogue still defaults to spot suppliers.

sections.heading: Options
sections.body:
Re-place the nine unconfirmed lines on the frameworks, and fix the catalogue default (preferred)
Cancel the nine unconfirmed lines at no cost and re-order them on FA-2025-PIPE-01 and FA-2025-VLV-02 at framework prices; let the five confirmed lines ship. Ask Procurement to have the catalogue default set back to the framework suppliers, so the next load does not repeat it.
Kept now: $0.30M · Secured after: $9.0M · 37.2% · Leak stopped: ≈ $2.6M a year · Crews held up: none
Trade-off: Leaves $0.26M of premium on the five confirmed lines, and rests on Harbor and Kestrel holding their quoted lead times.

Re-place all 14, including the five confirmed lines
Cancel the nine unconfirmed lines and ask Northgate and Ridgeline to take back the five confirmed ones at up to 5% restocking; re-order all 14 on the frameworks and fix the catalogue.
Kept now: $0.46M after restocking · Secured after: $9.16M · 37.9% · Restocking: up to $0.09M · Needs suppliers to agree: 5 lines
Trade-off: About $0.17M more, but it needs two spot suppliers to agree, and three of the confirmed pipe lines are already picked for delivery this week.

Let this batch stand and fix the catalogue only
Keep the 14 orders as placed; change the catalogue default so the next orders go to the frameworks.
Kept now: $0 · Premium paid: $0.55M · Leak stopped: ≈ $2.6M a year · Disruption: none
Trade-off: No change for nine project teams, but the $0.55M is paid and the secured figure does not move.
